sections.h2: Sale routes for a Concord owner on a short clock
sections.html:
You can hire an agent, run the sale yourself, or sign with a company that pays cash and takes the house untouched. Owners usually choose after weighing their deadline, the shape of the roof and mechanicals, and how many strangers they want walking through.

An agent exposes the property to the most buyers, though you clean, stage and then wait for a lender to approve the purchaser. Cash gives up some price in return for a closing day you pick. Concord is in Cabarrus County northeast of Charlotte, so buyers often shop both sides of the county line.

  • Agent route: strongest for a tidy house and a seller who can wait a month or two.
  • Do-it-yourself route: skips a commission but leaves pricing, forms and haggling to you.
  • Cash route: a fit for estates, neglected maintenance, empty houses and tight deadlines.

All three end with the deed recorded in Cabarrus County's land records. State recording law treats the moment of registration as the point that protects the new owner against creditors and later purchasers.

Concord is the county seat of Cabarrus County and its largest city, with a mid-2025 estimate of 114,598 people. The count went from 79,066 in 2010 to 105,240 in 2020, and the latest estimate runs 8.8 percent over the 2020 base. Founders marked out the town in 1796, and a Cannon Mills founder's home on Union Street North, finished in 1928, points to a textile past.

About two in three Concord homes house their owners, so most buyers expect to move in themselves. Households average 2.78 people, a family-sized figure, and a 26.9 minute commute hints that plenty of residents work beyond city limits. Median household income is $86,921.

sections.h2: Who bills property tax on a Concord house
sections.html:
The county appraises every parcel and sends the bill, with city and fire district levies riding on it. Its collections staff handle the county, seven municipalities and 16 fire districts, and each government fixes its rate during budget season ending June 30.

Values are broken into land, building and extras like sheds, pools, fences and driveways, and the current values reflect January 1, 2024. Since the combined rate shifts with the city and fire district, ask Tax Administration what applies to your parcel.

  • Listing window: first business day of January to January 31.
  • Bill due date: September 1.
  • Late interest starts on January 6.

State law charges 2 percent for the rest of January and three quarters of a percent per month after that. The lien reaches back to the January listing date, so your closing attorney should confirm the year is settled before funds move.

Talk to the county's Tax Revaluation office first, and move up to the Board of Equalization and Review (BER) only if that fails. Your request must be in hand before that board adjourns, normally in late April.

Informal talks begin in January. The board itself sits sometime from the first Monday of April to the first Monday of May. Paper filings, mailed forms and the online system all work, with evidence attached, and a Notice of Real Estate Assessed Value gives you 30 days to answer.

  1. Informal sit-down with an appraiser.
  2. BER hearing before local residents.
  3. State Property Tax Commission, 30 days after the board's notice.
  4. Appellate courts, where counsel is required.

Call the Revaluation office for the current filing address, hours and forms.

sections.h2: Property tax relief for Concord owners
sections.html:
The state runs three relief programs and lets an owner pick one. They serve older or disabled owners, a disabled veteran, and lower-income owners through a circuit breaker. File Form AV-9 with the county assessor, with June 1 before the tax year as the cutoff.

  • Older or disabled owners: part of the value is excluded when income is under a yearly-adjusted limit.
  • Disabled veteran: a fixed amount of value is excluded, and the form sets no age or income condition.
  • Circuit breaker: the bill is capped at a share of income and the rest is deferred.

Deferred tax comes due when the home transfers, so a sale repays up to three earlier years. The AV-9 form lists the current dollar limits.

sections.h2: Recording and transfer costs at closing
sections.html:
Deed excise tax is the seller's cost, collected by the register's office. The state rate is one dollar per $500 of value, rounded up.

Filing fees are separate, set by the state at the same level in every county, with a surcharge for added pages. Recording the release of an old mortgage is free. Request a tax payoff from the collector and walk through the settlement statement with the closing attorney.

Zoning and permit history belong to City of Concord Planning and Development Services, and building permit files come from Cabarrus County. Gather papers for additions, decks and finished basements, because a lender or inspector may request them.

If your likely buyer wants a carriage house or nightly rentals, get the planning staff's reading of the development ordinance for your lot in writing. Older homes near downtown deserve an extra question: ask the planning office whether any historic review touches exterior work on your block.

sections.h2: Cash offer versus listing in Concord
sections.html:
With a median owned-home value of $353,700, a repair estimate matters. Get written quotes for a roof, HVAC or plumbing problem, add what you would spend carrying the house for a few months, and set that against a cash bid. A cash buyer will take the house untouched, but expects to be paid for that convenience with a lower price.

A house in good shape can do well on the open market, especially with buyers moving between Concord and Charlotte. If time or condition is the problem, a firm closing day may be worth more than the extra dollars.

sections.h2: Inherited, behind on payments or rented
sections.html:
State law puts a clock on each situation. Note the date on every notice you hold first.

  • Foreclosure: a clerk of superior court hears the case, and a higher bid can follow the sale.
  • Inheritance: small estates may use an affidavit, and the state's estate tax is repealed.
  • Tenants: notice lengths depend on the tenancy type.

Hand any buyer the lease early and have a North Carolina attorney read it with you.

sections.h2: Preparing a Concord house for a quick sale
sections.html:
Assemble the paperwork a buyer will want before the first phone call. A thin folder costs days at the table.

  • Deed, payoff letter from your lender, and the newest county tax bill.
  • Permit and inspection records for decks, additions or finished rooms.
  • Leases, with the tenant's contact details and payment record.
  • Contractor quotes for roof, HVAC or plumbing work.

With those ready you can set a listing, a self-sale and a cash offer side by side and choose by your own deadline. Judge each by what you net after the payoff, the deed tax and any repair credits.

faqs.q: Do cash buyers in Concord accept a house with problems?
faqs.a: Yes, they buy as is, while a conventional buyer may ask for credits after inspection. Collect quotes so you can compare both outcomes.

faqs.q: Which office mails a Concord tax bill?
faqs.a: Cabarrus County, whose collections staff cover the county, seven municipalities and 16 fire districts.

faqs.q: Is there a state deed tax on a Concord sale?
faqs.a: Yes. The seller owes one dollar per $500 of value on filing the deed.

faqs.q: When does the Cabarrus County bill fall due?
faqs.a: September 1, with interest avoided if you pay before January 6.

faqs.q: Where does a Concord value appeal go?
faqs.a: To the Cabarrus County Tax Revaluation office, in writing or online, before the BER adjourns.
